body:
Suggestions related to this:
- Prominently located (on angular.io), clear statement of intended browser/version compatibility / support.
- Make the first party published (i.e. on angular.io) quickstarts/examples/etc include any necessary polyfills or other accommodations, to work across the list of supported browsers.
- Make the official-endorsed CLI create projects, by default, which work across the list of supported browsers.
- Gently urge the community to do the same, to increase the chances that people who pick up initial A2 examples from places other than angular.io, also by default include any necessary accommodations to work across the list of supported browsers.

Fwiw a warning in the docs has been added, see the PR https://github.com/angular/angular.io/pull/1999. You can check the website in the docs for pipes 

> The Date and Currency pipes need the ECMAScript Internationalization API. Safari and other older browsers don't support it. We can add support with a polyfill.
@laskoviymishka thanks for initiating this issue. I'm back at work today and will take a look.

issue.body:
Running unit tests in non-Chrome browsers raised some doubts about this API which is currently used in the Date and Currency pipes.

To start with, it is not supported in all Safari versions (desktop and mobile) and older browsers:
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl
http://caniuse.com/#search=intl

Then, on browsers which support it, the result doesn't match what Chrome does. 
On Firefox, one of the test fires this 2 years old bug: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=866372
On IE11, most tests are failing due to discrepancies in output (formatting, white space, special chars,etc).

At the end of the day, it seems only reliable in Chrome, but it is also difficult to polyfill.
So, if anyone has a good solution to that, please speak up!

body: There's a lightweight alternative to moment.js - https://date-fns.org/

After going over issues touching i18n-related pipes (mostly date / time formatting one) I'm more and more convinced that the current way of providing custom formats on top of `Intl` API is problematic. There is a proposal that aims at addressing custom formats as part of the `Intl` API (https://github.com/zbraniecki/proposal-intl-formatToParts) and when implemented (or sth similar) would allow us to have proper solution. The current approach of parsing output of the `Intl` API is flawed and the #12632 is the best prof of this.

I'm not sure what the best approach is and open options include:
* pushing standardization of `formatToParts` and suggesting a polyfill till then
* dropping `Intl` API in favour of sth else (hand rolled solution or well-known library like moment.js)

I'm still gathering all the issues and listing open options but till this process is over and it is clear what are the next steps  we won't merge any new PRs that change API surface.

> hand rolled solution

don't think it will be better than Intl :)

body: @pkozlowski-opensource using moment js is not a good option for a common piece of framework, neither hand rolled solution would not work. `DateTimeFormat.prototype.formatToParts` looks really promising, but for now it easier to just implement you own pipe on top of moment js rather than jumping around `Intl` api and built-in date pipe. May be it worth to extract all this formatting pipes from common to something more flexible as a separate npm package, so it could update more frequently.
